result.rationale: Post#cook returns raw verbatim for raw_html cook_method ('return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]'), and TopicEmbed.import passes feed/article HTML as post raw with that cook method, bypassing Sanitize. poll_feed applies CGI.unescapeHTML to feed content, reconstituting escaped entities into live tags. The embed view renders '<%= raw post.cooked %>' in an iframe with X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL. Attackers controlling feed/content thus get stored XSS on the forum origin.

judged_text: TopicEmbed.import stores third-party feed/article HTML as the post raw with cook_method raw_html (which Post#cook returns verbatim), so the markup never passes through the normal Discourse Sanitize pipeline, and poll_feed even applies CGI.unescapeHTML to feed content, converting escaped entities into live tags. Whatever controls feed_polling_url content (or the arbitrary t[:link] URLs the disqus task fetches) gets stored XSS on the forum origin: script tags execute in the server-rendered embed iframe (framed with X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL), and event-handler attributes execute when forum users open the imported topic in the regular view.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `raw_html` cook path that bypasses normal cooking/sanitization: `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and sets `raw` to feed/article HTML (`absolutize_urls(url, contents)`), with no sanitization step (app/models/topic_embed.rb). `Jobs::PollFeed` further calls `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, which can turn escaped entities back into live markup before importing (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). The embed rendering uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), so any injected tags/attributes in imported content would be rendered/executed. This is a verifiable XSS risk introduced by the diff.
